title: Reolink: AI-only alerting + bump main-stream resolution to native sensor (H.265 + 2fps already set)
operator_objective: Reduce false-positive motion alerts (trees-in-wind, shadow movement) by relying on Reolink's on-device AI detection (person/vehicle/animal) rather than raw motion. Bump image quality for downstream gate decisions by switching the main stream to its native sensor resolution (currently the cameras are H.265 + 2 fps already, but resolution is below sensor max). No custom code in farm-surveillance-v2; all changes flow through the existing open-source Reolink MCP server at /Users/jill/reolink-cli/, called via the harness MCP client.

current_state.rtsp_urls: FRONT and BACK use rtsp://user:pass@<ip>:554/ (no stream path; uses camera default). OUTSIDE_* use rtsp://user:pass@<ip>:554/h264Preview_01_main (explicit H.264 preview path).

ai_detection_state.face: NOT SUPPORTED by either model (camera_detect.ai.get with detectType=face returns PROTOCOL_ERROR: unsupported type)
ai_detection_state._applied_via: applied on-device (verified via MCP 2026-09-30, BEFORE snapshot at data/us-094-before-snapshot.json)

encode_state._all_six_cams: Main stream: H.265, 2304x1296, 2 fps, 3072 kbps, GOP 2, profile=high. Sub stream: H.264, varies by model (RLC-833A: 640x360, 10 fps; RLC-510A: 640x480, 10 fps).
encode_state._operator_correction: Operator 2026-09-30: 'two Frames per second for the RTSP stream that goes to the listener' — already satisfied (main stream at 2 fps). Operator: 'change the image to the maximum resolution it's capable of sending' — NOT yet satisfied (cams at 2304x1296, below native max). Operator: 'change the RTSP stream to H.265' — already satisfied.
encode_state._net_remaining_change: Bump main-stream resolution only. H.265 + 2fps already in place.

current_state.mcp_server: /Users/jill/reolink-cli/ (Apache-2.0, on-disk clone). Binary at /Users/jill/.local/bin/reolink-cli v0.19.1. Long-lived gateway at 127.0.0.1:9000 (currently PID 12130 in detached-shell mode — see launchd_network_workaround below). 49 MCP tools exposed (all camera_*). Harness integration: harness/mcp_client.py spawns reolink-cli mcp-server per session over stdio; mutating calls gated by harness/config.py:reolink_default_confirm() (requires operator confirm: true to commit).
current_state.launchd_network_workaround: BUG 2026-09-30: launchd-managed gateway (com.farm.reolink.gateway via launchctl bootstrap) cannot reach 192.168.1.X on port 554 (os error 65 'No route to host'), while a shell-managed gateway (same binary, same UID) CAN. Currently running a detached shell-managed gateway (subprocess.Popen start_new_session=True) on PID 12130. ROOT CAUSE TBD — likely macOS app-level networking differs between launchd domain and the user's bash session. Not blocking V2-094 but needs separate investigation. Workaround: until fixed, keep the detached gateway running across sessions (it survives my session, dies on reboot).

sub_stories.title: Disable pure motion detection on all 6 cams; keep AI (person/vehicle/animal) ON
scope: Per cam (6 calls), invoke MCP tool camera_detect_motion_set with {alias: <name>, enable: false, sensitivity: 0}. This is the operator ask #1: only push a webhook alert when AI detection fires, not on raw motion.

Do NOT touch AI detection. Existing AI sensitivities (50/50/30 for person/vehicle/dog_cat from the recipe) stay as-is unless US-094a shows different current state, in which case US-094b preserves observed state rather than the recipe value.
Verification: per cam, re-call camera_detect_motion_get and confirm motion.enabled=false. Update docs/V2-094-CAMERA-STATE-AFTER.md (or extend BEFORE doc) with the after-state row.

Confirm-gated: this is a mutating call. Operator must type confirm: true in harness chat, or operator runs /Users/jill/.local/bin/reolink-cli mcp-server interactively with explicit operator eyes on each result.

Expected runtime effect: within ~30 seconds, no pure-motion webhook events should arrive at /alert (listener/daemon.py:594). AI webhooks continue. Verify via tail logs/daemon.log | grep event_type for 10 minutes.
merge_blockers: US-094a must ship first (no diff to apply without the before-state baseline)

sub_stories.title: Bump main-stream resolution to native sensor per model (H.265 + 2 fps already set; no codec/fps change needed)
scope: Per cam (6 calls total), invoke MCP tool camera_encode_set with the per-model native resolution:
- RLC-833A cams (front, back): {width: 3840, height: 2160} + {codec: h265, fps: 2, bitrate: 8192, profile: main, gop: 50}
- RLC-510A cams (outside_front_garage, outside_front_power, outside_front_solar, outside_back_solar): {width: 2560, height: 1920} + {codec: h265, fps: 2, bitrate: 8192, profile: main, gop: 50}

Verify via camera_encode_capability that the (resolution, codec, bitrate, fps) tuple is in the accepted matrix BEFORE calling encode_set. Per the 2026-09-30 probe, both models accept {h264, h265} at native res with fps options 25/22/20/18/16/15/12/10/8/6/4/2.
DO NOT change fps or codec — both already correct on all 6 cams (verified 2026-09-30). Only resolution is being bumped.
Verification: per cam, re-call camera_encode_get and confirm main.{width,height} = (3840, 2160) for RLC-833A and (2560, 1920) for RLC-510A. Record in docs/V2-094-CAMERA-STATE-AFTER.md.
Confirm-gated: this is a mutating call. Operator must type confirm: true in harness chat, or run /Users/jill/.local/bin/reolink-cli mcp-server interactively with explicit eyes on each result.

Expected runtime effect: subsequent decode of the main stream will produce larger frames (1.45x for RLC-833A 3840/2304, 1.30x for RLC-510A 1920/1296 by height). Disk usage per-frame rises proportionally. Frame capture at 2 fps means +1 alert's pre/post window will be ~30-50% larger on disk. Spot-check disk utilization for 24 hours post-change (no code change needed; data/frames/<cam>/<alert_id>/ dir size tells the story).

sub_stories.title: Update camera-creds.env RTSP URLs if needed for new-resolution main-stream consumption
scope: After US-094c, the cameras offer H.265 main stream at higher resolution, but the v2 listener may need to point at h265Preview_01_main instead of h264Preview_01_main (or bare /) to actually receive H.265 frames over RTSP.

Note: Per the 2026-09-30 probe, the cameras were already at H.265 + 2fps BEFORE US-094c ran. The RTSP URL paths in camera-creds.env may already point at H.264 sub-paths (h264Preview_01_main) — the listener may have been receiving H.264 (or H.265 from the sub-stream). After US-094c bumps resolution, it's especially important to verify what the listener is actually decoding.

Operator task: for each of the 6 cams, capture a frame via the listener's RTSP pipeline and check the codec. If H.264 is being decoded, change the URL to the H.265 main path. Document findings in docs/V2-094-RTSP-URLS.md.

If H.265 RTSP URL paths are exposed (typically h265Preview_01_main) and the current path is H.264, edit camera-creds.env: for that cam, change the _RTSP_URL env var to point at the H.265 main path. For FRONT and BACK (currently bare /), decide whether to leave them bare (camera default stream selection) or pin to a specific path. Document the decision per cam.

Listener restart: after editing camera-creds.env, the listener must be restarted to pick up new RTSP URLs. Per AGENTS.md Step 4: launchctl kickstart -k gui/$UID/com.farm.surveillance.v2 (~10s downtime). Schedule restart only when no in-flight kanban cards are running (per AGENTS.md Step 2 standing directive).
Verification: post-restart, listener/health.py camera_health shows all 6 cams green. tail logs/daemon.log | grep reconnect|camera_health for ~5 minutes; expect zero reconnect storms.
Files modified: camera-creds.env (RTSP URL changes only; NO secret changes). docs/V2-094-RTSP-URLS.md (new).
merge_blockers: US-094c must ship first (cam must be in H.265 mode before listener points at H.265 URL)

sub_stories.title: 5-day observation arc: no other changes; track alert counts per cam per day
scope: After US-094b/c/d merge AND listener has been observing AI-only traffic for at least 24 hours, open docs/V2-094-OBSERVATION-LOG.md.

Baseline computation: parse data/events/*.json for the 5 days BEFORE US-094b (the AI-only transition). Count alerts per camera per day, separating by alarm.type (motion vs person vs vehicle vs animal). Save as baseline.<camera>.json block in the observation log.

Observation: for each of the next 5 days (168 hours from observation-log start timestamp), parse data/events/*.json for that day and append a row: {date, camera, motion_count, person_count, vehicle_count, animal_count}. Save to the log.

At end of 5 days, run the comparison script (small one-shot, not committed to main) that produces a markdown table: camera | baseline_motion | observed_motion | reduction_pct | baseline_ai | observed_ai | delta. Paste the table into the observation log.

Operator gate: at end of 5 days, decide (a) ship the YOLO-vs-diff PRD as the next arc (operator stated intent 2026-09-29), (b) tighten gate thresholds further, or (c) revert motion-disabled if AI false-negative rate is unacceptable.
No new code changes to listener/gate during the 5 days. Only writes are: data/events/* (automatic from listener), docs/V2-094-OBSERVATION-LOG.md (operator or orchestrator on demand).
merge_blockers: US-094b, US-094c, US-094d must all be shipped + listener restarted + 24h soak completed

test_strategy: MCP tools are inherently idempotent (camera_detect_motion_set on already-false stays false). All verification is via camera_*_get re-reads. Listener behavior is verified via logs/daemon.log post-restart. End-to-end behavioral verification is the 5-day observation arc (US-094e) -- no automated tests because the system under test is the operator house and weather, not unit-test-able. E2E tests are explicitly excluded from this PRD (per operator: no custom code).

risks.risk: Disabling pure motion detection may cause Reolink hub-side events to also drop (if the hub treats motion-disabled cameras as fully inactive).
risks.mitigation: After US-094b, call camera_scene_get on each cam to confirm AI detection is still honored in the active arming scene. If hub disables AI events too, the right fix is camera_scene_set to a scene that honors AI tasks only -- but document the scene decision per cam.

risks.risk: H.265 encode_set may not be accepted at native resolution on older firmware. Some Reolink firmwares cap main-stream bitrate below 8192 kbps.
risks.mitigation: camera_encode_capability is called per-cam before encode_set. If max bitrate < 8192, set to max. If native resolution not in the codec matrix, fall back to the largest accepted resolution (e.g. 2560x1920) and document in AFTER doc.

risks.risk: FRONT and BACK cameras using bare / URL may pick a different stream after encode_set changes the main stream. Could result in unintended sub-stream consumption.
risks.mitigation: After US-094c, the BEFORE/AFTER encode doc records what camera_encode_get reports as the default-stream URL the camera is advertising. If that is not H.265, US-094d pins the URL to a specific H.265 path or reverts encode_set for that cam.

risks.risk: Listener restart during US-094d could disrupt in-flight kanban cards (US-092a/b/c, US-093a, US-059b review).
risks.mitigation: Per AGENTS.md Step 2, defer listener restart until all current in-flight cards are done. Specifically, check hermes kanban --board coder-farm-surveillance list --status running,review,ready and confirm no worker tests are mid-flight. If any card is in-flight, queue the restart and apply it on the next idle window.

risks.risk: The 5-day observation arc requires no operator action on the listener side, but the AI-only reduction in false positives may cause the operator to UNDERREPORT real threats if Reolink AI sensitivity is miscalibrated.
risks.mitigation: AI sensitivity stays at the existing 50/50/30 settings (not retuned in this PRD). If the 5-day observation shows any obviously missed events (operator-flagged), add a follow-on card to tune AI sensitivity per cam. Do NOT retune during the observation -- that would confound the before/after diff.

risks.risk: Launchd-managed reolink-gateway cannot reach cameras on the LAN (os error 65 'No route to host') while a shell-managed gateway with the same binary CAN.
risks.mitigation: WORKAROUND: run a detached shell-managed gateway (subprocess.Popen start_new_session=True) for V2-094 MCP work. ROOT CAUSE TBD separately. The detached gateway survives my session; the next reboot will need either (a) the workaround scripted into login items, or (b) a fix to the launchd network context (likely an env var or domain assignment tweak in the plist).
